feature_candidates.description: Log-scaled normalized exposure count per video derived from leaky video stats, centered by tab mean.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Potential small rank gain if exposure correlates with popularity, but risk of leakage-driven overfitting; likely flat once controlling for tab.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Compute per-video log count on train+valid; store as static feature; apply log1p and standardize; use only in hypothesis tests.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: High: includes future exposure counts; must never be trusted for final ranking.
feature_candidates.name: log_video_exposure_count_scaled

feature_candidates.description: Per-user historical long_view ratio over video_type or upload_type categories, smoothed with prior.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Moderate positive gain by capturing preference homogeneity; avoids user-only constant issue.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Compute from train log only: group by user + video_type, count long_view/total; add smoothing (e.g., Bayesian prior).
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if derived strictly from train; no future info.
feature_candidates.name: user_videotype_longview_ratio

feature_candidates.description: Encoded tab with relative position (e.g., rank of exposure within user's tab sequence) to capture recency-context.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Small gain by capturing position effects that are not user-constant; but must avoid raw row order leakage.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: From train log, compute per-user sequential index per tab and normalize; embed as numeric/embedding feature.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if computed from train sequence; do not use raw row order beyond training period.
feature_candidates.name: tab_interaction_position

findings.evidence: DATA CARD Tab Breakdown shows long_view rates 38.61% (tab1), 4.22% (tab0), 48.93% (tab4).
findings.implication: A tab-context feature could help rank within user, but careful with sparse tab handling and confounds with position.
findings.observation: Long_view rate varies strongly by tab (e.g., tab 4 ~49%, tab 0 ~4%), but tabs are sparse (top 3 tabs cover ~96% of rows).
findings.title: Tab-driven long_view rate separation

findings.evidence: DATA CARD Leakage Flag: 12.83B vs 2.62M exposures, ratio ~4892:1.
findings.implication: Any features from it may overfit future exposure; use only for hypothesis testing with explicit caveat, prefer log-derived counts.
findings.observation: Video statistics table aggregates full-platform traffic (ratio ~4892:1 vs logged), observation periods exceed log span.
findings.title: Video stats table is leaky and noisy

findings.evidence: DATA CARD lists user features; history_features family is registered.
findings.implication: Item-conditioned history (e.g., user's long_view rate on similar video_type) can add rank signal without leakage.
findings.observation: Per-user long_view/click/like/follow history from train is fully available; user-only constants are useless for within-user but history features vary by item.
findings.title: User-side history is likely discriminative

expected_artifacts: A compact EDA report (markdown) summarizing per-tab long_view trends and selected strong/uninformative features.
A leakage-aware feature candidate list with expected family compatibility and predicted primary metric impact.
A scatter/heatmap of video stats vs. observed long_view rates (train-only) to quantify noise.
A short recommendation for the next experiment (e.g., bpr with a new history feature or multi-task joint loss).
feature_hypotheses: Relative video popularity within a user's exposed set (rank-normalized view/long_view counts) is stable and adds gain under bpr.
User's historical long_view ratio on similar video types (video_type, upload_type) is predictive due to preference homogeneity.
Tab-specific long_view rates combined with position in user history encode context that is currently untapped.
Deriving normalized exposure frequency per video from the video stats table after log-scaling and centering reduces leakage-driven overfitting while preserving signal.
leakage_risks: Any feature derived from the video statistics table includes future exposure counts; must be caveated and only used for hypothesis testing, not trusted for leak-free ranking.
Using video stats to compute per-user normalization could leak rank information across users if not strictly computed within the exposed set.
Duplicate rows (15,609) and zero-duration videos (239) may bias interaction-pattern summaries; need to exclude or explicitly account.
Hour/tab interactions may be confounded with position; must avoid using row order as a feature except as a historical sequence feature.
plan.objective: Design a leakage-safe EDA pass to identify discriminative, within-user-rankable signals for long_view ranking, targeting GAUC/nDCG@5 improvement over baseline 0.6016.
questions: How do long_view rates vary by video/user interaction recency, dwell-time proxies, and sequential position within a user's session?
Which user-side signals (e.g., active degree, follow/comment history, long_view history) are most predictive when combined with video-side statistics in within-user rank?
Does the leaky video statistics table provide statistically separable signal after controlling for tab and hour?
What is the marginal rank predictive power of per-video exposure counts, tab affinity, and cross-video transition counts from the log itself?
required_inputs: Train and validation logs with existing features (user_active_degree, video_type, upload_type, tab, hourmin, duration, play metrics).
The video statistics aggregate table (explicitly caveated as leaky) for cross-tab exploration.
Precomputed per-user history features (clicks, long_view, like, follow) from train split only.
Current baseline config and registered family definitions (bpr, group_softmax, history_features, multi_task) for compatibility checks.
